text:
maria: spinning up a focused canary for peko-18b:int4 to debug allocation spikes. seeing ~12% coldstart OOMs across a handful of nodes; posting traces to /stackdumps.
sam: is it OOM during model load, kv priming, or prefetch allocate?
maria: fails during prefetch + kv priming path. allocator reports cannot satisfy a ~200MB allocation then GPU OOM.
kai: any correlation with request shapes? long prompts + large max_new?
maria: yes. most repros: prompt ~900-1200 tokens + max_new_tokens left as default 1024.
leah: 1024 default + prefetch reserve is a disaster on int4. we normally use 256/512 for 18B.
noah: can you paste the canary config?
maria: canary runtime cfg: service.default_max_new_tokens=1024, prefetch.enabled=true, prefetch.reserve_ratio=0.2, prefetch.strategy=eager.
sam: reserve 0.2 * 1024 = 204 tokens reserved per request. with concurrency=3 that
~600 tokens reserved concurrently per slot.
kai: and int4 kernels have small slab block sizes -> big fragmentation risk.
leah: propose immediate canary changes: (1) reduce default_max_new_tokens to 256 for peko canary. (2) set prefetch.reserve_ratio=0.08. (3) switch prefetch.strategy to windowed for canary. (4) enable soft-kv-evict after 150ms idle.
maria: ran a microbench: old defaults p50=130ms p95=720ms tokens/s=175; new defaults 256+reserve0.08 p50=98ms p95=360ms tokens/s=215; zero OOMs in 300 runs.
noah: nice. any quality impact? shorter default only limits max allowed generation; won't truncate existing short answers. but callers that expect long outputs need route-level config.
sam: add a per-route flag allow_long_gen=true to preserve old behavior for opt-in. also add a runtime guard: if prompt_len + req.max_new > 1600 => require explicit allow_long_gen or route goes to dedicated capacity.
kai: quant team: can we change slab allocator to larger superblocks for peko int4? that will reduce fragmentation at the cost of a bit more baseline waste.
quant-bot: noted. opened issue rw-quant/peko#19 "superblock allocator + int4 fragmentation". tagging @quant-team.
leah: ops items: (A) push canary config delta (maria) (B) instrument fragment_ratio and OOM_count per-host (sam) (C) add defrag hook between heavy sessions (infra) (D) doc per-route override and safety gating (leah).
infra-bot: deploy job queued: canary/prefetch-tweak (cj-5865). will report status.
sam: for a fast mitigation add a periodic compaction call after N requests: run lightweight compaction kernel and cudaDeviceSynchronize to coalesce free lists.
maria: test repro snippet for loadtool: POST /v1/generate {"model":"peko-18b-int4","prompt":"<~1000 tokens>","max_new_tokens":1024,"prefetch":true} use concurrency 3.
noah: also saw mem fragmentation creeping up across sessions; add a rolling GC threshold: if frag_ratio > 0.65 then trigger compaction and lower prefetch reserve for new sessions.
leah: I will draft a short customer note about default change and mention opt-in for long generations.
kai: long-term: adjust kernel alloc path to coalesce tiny allocations and prefer pooled buffers for KV and prefetch to avoid many small allocations.
maria: agreed. roll the canary tweaks, monitor OOM_count and fragment_ratio for 24h, then decide to roll to dedicated. thanks team :thumbsup:
